title: 4521-MOM-LOI-039-062-0001-GAR rev01 Performance Test Procedure
summary:
- The document outlines a performance test procedure for Oil to Salt heat exchangers.
- It aims to determine thermal balance, pressure drop, HAT/CAT values, and OHTC/Duty/Pressure loss.
- The calculation method uses correction factors based on ASME PTC 12.5 standards.
- Stakeholders must agree on testing responsibilities, reference conditions, and inspection criteria before starting the test.
- LOINTEK is responsible for analysis of results and issuance of reports.
- Four variables are measured for thermal calculation of the system.
- ASME PTC 12.5 is used to determine the accuracy of calculations.
- Client and Lointek will decide which measurements are most reliable.
- Heat exchanger must operate at steady state conditions before starting tests.
- Two measurements must be performed for repeatability.
- Fouling coefficient can be reviewed based on direct observation.
- Sizing of heat exchangers is based on nominal design case.
summary_points: The document outlines a performance test procedure for Oil to Salt heat exchangers.
It aims to determine thermal balance, pressure drop, HAT/CAT values, and OHTC/Duty/Pressure loss.
The calculation method uses correction factors based on ASME PTC 12.5 standards.
Stakeholders must agree on testing responsibilities, reference conditions, and inspection criteria before starting the test.
LOINTEK is responsible for analysis of results and issuance of reports.
Four variables are measured for thermal calculation of the system.
ASME PTC 12.5 is used to determine the accuracy of calculations.
Client and Lointek will decide which measurements are most reliable.
Heat exchanger must operate at steady state conditions before starting tests.
Two measurements must be performed for repeatability.
Fouling coefficient can be reviewed based on direct observation.
Sizing of heat exchangers is based on nominal design case.
Total thermal duty and outlet temperatures are recalculated with new fouling factors.
Instruments installed during assembly are used to calculate the performance of the exchanger.
Accuracy should meet or exceed the uncertainty of results obtained.
Include a plane of the tubesheet in Annex A for plugged tubes.
Conduct a tracing of general behavior before final performance test.
Install thermometers, manometers, and mass flow meters at inlet/outlet of hot/cold fluids.
Perform measures during performance testing with specific conditions.
